caption: Boiling water is poured into a thick glass tumbler taken straight from the fridge, and the glass cracks with a sharp snap.

sa.check: A glass tumbler that reads as cold: frost or condensation on it.
Boiling water is poured into the tumbler.
A crack appears in the glass.
The crack runs through the glass.
The glass may split and leak.
The pour comes first and the crack follows.

pc.expect: The glass is a brittle solid: a crack runs through it as a sharp line and the glass stays rigid, splitting rather than bending.
pc.fail: The glass bends or sags instead of cracking; or the glass stretches as the water goes in; or the glass crumbles to powder; or the crack closes and the glass flexes back.

pc.expect: The crack stays in the glass and any pieces stay as pieces; the glass does not heal.
pc.fail: The crack closes and the glass is whole again; or a piece that fell away reappears joined to the glass; or a second tumbler appears; or the glass vanishes.

pc.expect: The crack appears after the hot water goes in and any water leaks out through the split.
pc.fail: The crack appears before the water reaches the glass; or the water goes in and the glass stays whole and unmarked to the end of the clip; or the glass splits open and the water stays in it with no leak.

pc.expect: The water falls downward into the tumbler and any leak runs down its outside and pools below.
pc.fail: The water travels upward from the kettle; or a leak runs up the glass; or the water climbs the glass's wall and stays above its level; or the leak hangs in the air beside the glass.

pc.expect: One tumbler; it stays a tumbler as it cracks and does not turn into another material.
pc.fail: The glass melts and drips; or the glass turns into another object; or the glass's shape changes without breaking; or the glass becomes a fabric that folds.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The counter, the kettle and the surroundings stay the same.
pc.fail: The counter changes pattern; or the kettle changes shape; or items around the glass rearrange.
